access_note: The spreadsheet is obtained through a short download form; the map, dashboards and summary tables are open.
description: The Global Nuclear Power Tracker from Global Energy Monitor (GEM), a non-profit research organisation, covers nuclear power units across all statuses: operating, retired, prospective and cancelled, from the first experimental reactors of the 1940s to planned small modular reactors. On 26 September 2026 the page counted about 1,825 units in 62 countries and areas, 408 GW operating and 396 GW prospective. Records give status, reactor technology, location, construction start date, capacity, owner and operator, and summary tables show additions, retirements and cancellations by year. The latest release was August 2026. Coverage is global. Access is through a free online tracker map, dashboards and summary tables, and the full data set is a spreadsheet downloadable through a short download form on GEM's site, under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: prospective units include early announcements, and status and dates change between releases. Simulation uses are hazard exposure of reactor sites, long-term capacity planning and deployment timeline analysis. Related records: data-gem-global-integrated-power-tracker combines GEM's power trackers and data-gem-global-energy-ownership-tracker maps owners.
